title: Helmsman operator upgrade fallback and state reconciliation for drift-induced PodCrashLoop
creator: Priya Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported pod CrashLoop and degraded API availability immediately after rolling the on-prem operator to v2.7. Investigations show the operator's post-upgrade hook augmented a customer-managed ConfigMap with a helper annotation. In clusters with strict admission and a validating webhook that enforces ownerReferences format, the augmentation produced an invalid ownerReferences entry which caused the operator's garbage-collection path to attempt invalid deletions, leading to controller loops and PodCrashLoop. Scope: 3 customers reported escalations (region: EU & US), one production cluster had sustained 6 minutes of degraded API before automatic replica healing. This ticket coordinates the hotfix release, upgrade fallback behavior, state reconciliation runbook, and post-mortem artifacts.

rollback_plan: Primary: Pause operator upgrades via helm-hook (helm upgrade --set operator.upgrade.enabled=false) and immediately roll back to v2.6 tag using helm rollback for affected releases. Secondary: Apply sandboxed controller patch that disables GC path (controller.garbageCollection.enabled=false) and restart pods. For customers who cannot rollback quickly, run reconciliation script that removes invalid ownerReferences and restores kube objects from etcd snapshot if necessary. Communication: Send rollback intent to customer 15 min before action and validate with support engineer.
test_plan: Unit: add tests for ownerReferences scrubber to reject/clean malformed owner refs
Integration: upgrade path 2.6->2.7->2.7.1 in ephemeral clusters with and without validating webhooks
E2E: deploy customer sample manifests (including intentionally drifted ConfigMaps) and assert no pod CrashLoop after operator restart
Canary: progressive rollout to 5% of Dedicated clusters for 1 hour, monitor GC latency and controller restarts before ramping to 100%
acceptance_criteria: Hotfix (v2.7.1) disables post-upgrade augmentation by default and provides a safe scrub of ownerReferences
No CrashLoop events or controller restart spikes for 24h in canary cohorts

Documentation and runbook updated; postmortem published within 5 working days
